newsitem.title: CANADA: Cott settles class action, Cadbury suit.
newsitem.headline: Cott settles class action, Cadbury suit.

text.p: Cott Corp said on Thursday it reached a settlement agreement with the plaintiffs in its previously disclosed U.S. class action securities litigation, which began in early 1994, at a net cost of US$1.3 million.
The cost, which excludes legal fees, will be accounted for as an expense in the fourth quarter of 1997, Cott said.
Cott also said it settled without monetary obligation its litigation with Cadbury Beverages Inc over Cott's use of the Cott name in the United States.

Under the terms of the settlement, Cott retains the right to use the name Cott in the United States for all purposes for which it is currently being used. This is subject to requirements to distinguish Cott's activities from Cadbury's proprietary "Cott" trademark in the United States for branded soft drinks.

Cott said although it believed the litigation was without merit and it remained confident in the validity of its defences, a settlement would be in the best interest of the company to avoid future expense and effort on the litigation.
